svg.title: Two Garments
svg.desc: A one-minute comic in 7 panels. Two columns side by side: The white robe and The fine linen, row for row. Panel 1 (Revelation 6:9-11): four martyrs in white robes looking up, under the altar of heaven. Caption: "Under the altar, the martyrs." John says: "Then they were each given a white robe and told to rest a little longer." Panel 2 (Revelation 19:7-8): the Bride standing in bright white linen, arms raised. Caption: "The Bride, made ready." John says: "It was granted her to clothe herself with fine linen, bright and pure." A strip joins the panels above: ἐδόθη, “it was given”: the same word for both garments. Panel 3 (Zechariah 3:3-4): Joshua in a ragged, stained garment, and an attendant holding out a clean white robe to him. Caption: "Joshua the high priest, in filthy garments." The angel says: "I have taken your iniquity away from you, and I will clothe you with pure vestments." Panel 4 (Revelation 19:8; Ephesians 2:10): a believer in white holding out a loaf to a poor man sitting by the road. Caption: "The deeds God prepared." John says: "For the fine linen is the righteous deeds of the saints." Paul says: "Good works, which God prepared beforehand." Panel 5 (1 Corinthians 3:15): a building of wood and straw burning, its builder walking out of it in a white robe with empty hands. Caption: "The work burns. The robe holds." Paul says: "He himself will be saved, but only as through fire." Note: "Robe and linen at the judgment seat: the study’s reading." Panel 6 (1 Corinthians 3:14): a building of gold, silver and precious stones standing whole in the fire, its builder in white holding up a gold wreath. Caption: "The work survives the fire." Paul says: "If the work that anyone has built on the foundation survives, he will receive a reward." Panel 7 (Isaiah 61:10): a believer in a white robe and the Bride in bright linen, side by side with arms raised in praise. Caption: "Worn together: Isaiah’s song." Isaiah says: "He has clothed me with the garments of salvation; he has covered me with the robe of righteousness." The point: Both garments are given. The robe is your standing, washed white by the Lamb and never burned; the linen is the deeds God prepared for you to walk in. Wear both as His gift (Revelation 6:11; 19:8; Ephesians 2:10).

svg.text: Both garments are given. The robe is your standing, washed white by the
Lamb and never burned; the linen is the deeds God prepared for you to
walk in. Wear both as His gift (Revelation 6:11; 19:8; Ephesians 2:10).
Panel 4’s bread is one example: Revelation names no
deed. The Bride is Revelation’s picture of God’s people.
